Re: Pre-service appeal of denial of lumbar fusion  
Member: Jordan Novak  
Member ID: W423994730  
Plan: Aetna Commercial/ACA — North Dakota  
Reference number: POC-570CD9F39B-59936  
Requested service: Lumbar fusion  
CPT: 22612  
Date of denial notice: August 18, 2026  

Dear Aetna Appeals Reviewer:

I am appealing Aetna’s denial of prior authorization for lumbar fusion, CPT 22612. The denial states that the submitted documentation was incomplete and did not allow a determination of medical necessity. I respectfully request that Aetna overturn the denial and authorize the requested surgery after reviewing the enclosed clinical documentation.

The records address the clinical information requested for spinal-surgery review:

- I have experienced 14 months of progressive lower-back and leg pain that has not been relieved by rest.
- I completed eight weeks of supervised physical therapy, including core stabilization and lumbar flexibility, from May 24, 2026, through July 19, 2026. I completed 20 visits, and the treatment and outcome are documented in the physical-therapy discharge note.
- I used NSAIDs for six months without adequate relief.
- A corticosteroid injection on May 29, 2026, produced only two weeks of partial relief.
- MRI and flexion-extension radiographs obtained July 6, 2026, show grade I degenerative spondylolisthesis at L4-L5, 5 mm of translation on flexion-extension, and severe central stenosis compressing the cauda equina.
- My symptoms and examination are consistent with neurogenic claudication and diminished sensation in both L5 dermatomes.
- I cannot stand or walk for more than 10 minutes before leg pain and heaviness force me to stop. The symptoms improve with sitting, demonstrating a substantial limitation in daily functioning and ambulation.
- There is no bowel or bladder dysfunction.
- I have no active infection or untreated substance use. My BMI is 29, and I am a non-smoker.

These records provide the duration of symptoms, failed conservative treatment, medication history, injection response, objective imaging, neurological findings, functional limitations, and relevant risk information needed to evaluate the request. They also identify the exact spinal level and the instability demonstrated on flexion-extension imaging.

Aetna’s publicly available spinal-surgery bulletin is identified as Clinical Policy Bulletin 0743, titled “Spinal Surgery: Laminectomy and Fusion.” The public policy page states that lumbar fusion for degenerative disc disease and other indications not listed as medically necessary is not medically necessary. My request is not based solely on nonspecific axial back pain or degenerative disc disease. It is based on documented L4-L5 degenerative spondylolisthesis with motion-related translation, severe central stenosis with cauda-equina compression, neurogenic claudication, sensory deficits, progressive symptoms, major walking and standing limitations, and failure of documented conservative treatment.

The publicly available policy text also describes the importance of ruling out other causes, correlating advanced imaging with the clinical findings, documenting failed conservative therapy, and documenting functional limitation for lumbar decompression-related procedures. The records submitted with this appeal address those issues: the MRI and radiographs document severe stenosis and the affected level; the examination documents neurogenic claudication and bilateral L5 sensory changes; the physical-therapy discharge note documents completed supervised therapy; the medication and injection history documents additional unsuccessful treatment; and the functional history documents the inability to stand or walk for more than 10 minutes.

Please review the enclosed records and reverse the denial. If Aetna believes additional information is required, please identify each missing document or clinical fact specifically and provide a reasonable opportunity to submit it before issuing a final adverse determination.

Because the denial was based on allegedly incomplete documentation, please also provide the precise version of the policy and any additional clinical-review criteria applied to this request, including the effective or last-revised date and the specific documentation considered missing. The public policy page did not provide a verifiable effective or last-revised date in the information available to me.

Please send the appeal determination in writing. I request authorization for the lumbar fusion at L4-L5, CPT 22612, as requested by Lindqvist, MD.

Sincerely,

Jordan Novak  
[Mailing address]  
[Telephone number]  
[Email address]
